In 2026 he won the inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship in the event. In the mile, he is the 2026 Commonwealth Games champion. In the 3000 metres, Kerr is the 2024 and 2026 world indoor champion. As a junior, Kerr won gold at the 2015 European Junior Championships. Kerr competed for the University of New Mexico from 2015 to 2018, winning three NCAA titles. In April 2017, he set a collegiate record in the 1500 metres that stood until May 2021. He turned professional in 2018 and joined the Brooks Beasts Track Club. In 2023, Sportscotland named him Scottish Sportsperson of the Year. == Early life and background == Kerr was born on 8 October 1997 in Edinburgh, Scotland. Kerr began running with the Edinburgh Athletics Club at the age of eight. He was educated at George Watson's College. At 16, he started reaching out to athletic coaches at colleges in the United States, aiming to compete in the National Collegiate Athletics Association (NCAA). PHOTO: REUTERS Published Jul 18, 2026, 11:01 PM Updated Jul 19, 2026, 06:31 PM Set as preferred source Listen Summarise Britain’s Josh Kerr set a new men’s mile world record of 3min 42.66sec at the London Diamond League, breaking a 24-year-old mark.
The record continues Britain’s rich mile history, with World Athletics president Sebastian Coe awarding Kerr US$50,000 and a commemorative book.
“It’s important for me to leave a legacy , I’m 28 years old and I’ve been doing this for a long time .” Kerr said that he knew from within the opening 100m that he was in world-record form.
“Josh is a world champion, he’s won gold medals, run records but the world mile record...

Devotion to the world-record bid has seen Kerr miss out on life with his extended family in Britain, while he has surrounded himself with a dedicated backroom staff including physiotherapists, mental coaches and even a “performance chef”.

“With the amount of talk that I did over the last six months, hopefully that hype was worth it to get in the stadium and hopefully live a moment that I’m going to hear about in 10 years’ time,” said Kerr, 28.
It’s time to bring this record into the modern era through training, technology and effort,” Kerr argued.
“It was an incredible moment, kudos to Josh,” said Armand Duplantis, who has set 15 pole vault world records in his career.
It was so impressive.” Kerr said that having the likes of Coe and Cram, who along with Ovett dominated the event from 1979 to 1993, as onlookers was an honour.
Kerr was paced by training partners and outpaced Olympic bronze medallist Yared Nuguse in front of a 60,000-strong crowd.
“Hopefully, someone in this stadium takes inspiration from what I did, goes out and breaks my record.

“Once my pacemakers got into their positions and the splits were exactly what they needed to be, it was just making sure that my mind was available to go down the river, flow with the punches that were thrown at me today.
“It’s an event the whole world knows and understands.
Roger Bannister is partly responsible for that,” he said, referring to the Englishman who ran the first sub-4min mile in 1954.
“Bringing the record back to where it belongs is what I wanted to do for the last six months,” he said.

Kerr detailed his pre-race preparations for all his rivals to see, including converting his bedroom in Albuquerque, New Mexico, into an altitude chamber to better benefit from the natural production of more oxygen-rich red blood cells.
American Yared Nuguse hung on to Kerr’s coat-tails before the latter pulled away at the 300m mark.
